attributes.residual: THE RECONSTRUCTION IS ALMOST CERTAINLY RIGHT AND STILL SCORED WORSE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A CAP AND NOT A PARK ON A GUESS. Three independent structural indicators all improved: frame 232 -> 248 = target EXACTLY; the (r1) slot set went from 7 displacements to 5, matching target's count, with 3 of the 5 identical (36, 240, 252); opcode multiset 21t -> 18t and instruction count 118 -> 119 against target 121. But real went 163 -> 168 and, measured directly, fuzzy went 73.3388% -> 71.9091%, so BOTH arbiters preferred the pre-session state and nothing was retained. REMAINING GAP AT THE POINT OF ABANDONMENT, precisely: ours [32, 36, 192, 240, 252] vs target [36, 108, 188, 240, 252] - we carry one extra 4-byte slot at the bottom (low_gap 24 vs target 28) and the middle slots sit 4 high, i.e. exactly 4 bytes need to move from the named-local area into the bottom reservation while the total stays 248. That is a single 4-byte quantum and the 8-byte ruler cannot resolve it, which is the honest reason this stopped: adding 4 to the helper would add 8 across its 2 sites (overshoot), and no 4-byte named local remains to shed. NOT TRIED, and the recommended next axis: vary the merged buffer's element count (buf[38] was chosen to conserve 18+20) against the helper's declaration set, since those two are the only knobs that move the 4-byte boundary independently. FAKEMATCH NOTE: the pre-session buf1[18]/buf2[20] split is reconstruction debt - the original plainly reused ONE scratch array (both are written by FixMLineText and read identically) - so the merged single-buffer form is the more faithful source even though it scored worse this pass.
